jobs.title: Program Director – Home Visiting & Family Strengthening Services
jobs.description:
Help Strengthen Families. Build Stronger Communities. Lead Meaningful Change.

At Yolo County Children's Alliance (YCCA), we believe every child deserves the opportunity to thrive. Our mission is to protect and empower children by strengthening families throughout Yolo County through family support, parent education, and community collaboration.

We're seeking a passionate, strategic, and collaborative Program Director – Home Visiting & Family Strengthening Services to lead two of YCCA's flagship programs that support children and families during some of life's most critical moments.

This is more than a management position-it's an opportunity to shape programs that improve outcomes for hundreds of families while leading a dedicated team of professionals committed to making a lasting difference.

What You'll Do

As Program Director, you'll provide strategic leadership and operational oversight for YCCA's Home Visiting and Family Strengthening Services, ensuring high-quality, family-centered programs that meet contract, accreditation, and community expectations. You'll:

Lead and mentor one Program Manager and three Program Supervisors
Oversee program quality, compliance, budgets, contracts, and performance
Support Healthy Families America accreditation and continuous quality improvement
Develop strong partnerships with hospitals, community organizations, funders, and government agencies
Manage reporting, evaluations, and grant deliverables
Represent YCCA at county, regional, state, and national collaborative meetings
Help identify and pursue new funding opportunities
Participate in executive leadership planning and organizational decision-making
Support community outreach and YCCA-sponsored events

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

Strong nonprofit or human services leadership experience
Experience supervising managers and multidisciplinary teams
Budget, grant, and contract management experience
Quality assurance and continuous improvement experience
Knowledge of home visiting, early childhood, maternal-child health, or family support services
Experience working with culturally diverse communities using strengths-based and trauma-informed approaches
Outstanding communication, leadership, and relationship-building skills
Strong analytical and reporting abilities
Ability to travel throughout Yolo County and occasionally throughout Northern California or out of state

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with Healthy Families America
Knowledge of child welfare, infant and child development, and parent-child attachment
Understanding of Protective Factors and trauma-informed care
Familiarity with Yolo County community resources

Why This Role Matters

Every day, your leadership helps strengthen families, support parents, improve child well-being, and expand access to vital community resources. You'll lead talented professionals, build lasting partnerships, and ensure programs continue to make a measurable impact across Yolo County.

If you're an experienced leader who believes strong families build strong communities, we'd love to hear from you.

Yolo County Children's Alliance is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to creating a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace where everyone is welcomed, valued, and respected.

County or State Required Documentation:
Due to the nature of this role that may involve interaction with youth or require YCCA meet certain guidelines stipulated in federal and state funding, a fingerprint and background check is required.

jobs.title: Associate Director of Development
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Essie Justice Group (Essie) is building grassroots power to dismantle the US incarceration system, the most egregious creator of racial and gender injustice of our time. We are a loving and powerful community of women with incarcerated loved ones. Our community includes cisgender women, transgender women, formerly incarcerated women, gender expansive people, elders, and young people.

After twelve years of building an active membership across California and beyond, Essie is deepening its base-building and leadership development strategies with the 1 in 4 women with incarcerated loved ones to propel bold decarceration agendas across the nation. We seek to transform the criminal legal system and create a Black feminist future rooted in care, equity, community safety, and liberation. In the midst of significant organizational growth, we are seeking an impact-driven and strategic Associate Director of Development to join our team.

As Essie grows, the Associate Director of Development will take the lead in managing the internal operations for our philanthropic efforts to support our work to end mass incarceration and build a Black feminist future. We see our donors as partners in this work, and the Associate Director of Development is a thoughtful and deliberate steward of these relationships. The Associate Director of Development is a strategic fundraising leader who is comfortable getting into the weeds while also balancing the strategic development of the team. They excel at crafting clear and compelling narratives that connect philanthropic partners and potential donors to meaningful movement work, think empathetically about their audiences, and are deeply motivated by a belief in the leadership development and liberation strategies of directly impacted people.

Core Responsibilities

Donor Program Design and Management - Help develop strategies and processes for identifying and engaging donors and nurturing and managing donor relationships.

Partner with the Interim Co-Executive Directors to establish benchmarks and goals for individual fundraising.
Iterate and oversee development infrastructure internally, including CRM features and advising on key changes to roles and make-up of our existing structures for stakeholder engagement.
Evaluate and recommend new funding opportunities in alignment with Essie’s strategic priorities and programmatic work.
Support in determining the key organizational accomplishments and aspirations we communicate in grant applications and reports.
Lead the design and management of prospect research and relevant relationship management processes.
Develop solicitation goals, cultivation strategies, and stewardship plans in a way that donors are respected, retained, and inspired to increase their support.
Develop and implement engagement strategies including, but not limited to: telephone outreach, email/mail outreach, personal visits, and small group activities.
Review and finalize grants and proposals.
Develop strategies and manage implementation of donation appeals (digital or print as strategically identified) including seasonal appeals (ex. end of year/holiday giving) and complementary fundraising appeals matching Essie’s campaigns and policy fights.
Track and report results of appeals and special campaigns, adjusting strategies as needed.

Donor Relationship Stewardship - Manage and facilitate Essie’s ongoing organizational relationships with individual donors, ensuring that they remain engaged in and inspired by Essie’s work.

Manage robust donor stewardship and cultivation touchpoints including personal thank yous, digital communications, and personalized outreach.
Prepare and distribute materials to communicate with supporters including thank you letters, event reports, and annual reports.
Ensure electronic donor records are current in the development database, including tracking moves for those within the major gifts portfolio.
Advise and prepare senior leadership for donor meetings as needed.
Manage the strategy and coordination of funder visits with Executive Leadership.
Facilitate connective and grant reporting funder calls as identified.
Lead the planning and management of donor events that combine political education and philanthropic action.

Team Leadership - Manage and evaluate team members and processes for success.

Co-hold the container of the staff team and contractors to support day-to-day development operations and achieve set organizational goals together.
Provide input on development process improvements, and work with teammates to refine collaborative systems as necessary.
Work collaboratively and consistently with other leaders at Essie to define strategic priorities, make decisions about unanticipated opportunities, and manage towards operational plan goals.
Manage departmental budgets and work systems, and co-build and manage a dynamic Communications & Partnerships staff team.
Embody and promote Essie culture and values internally and externally.
Directly manage 1-2 staff members.

Who We’re Looking For

Ideal Qualifications

5+ years of development-related work experience, including experience with individual giving campaigns and direct responsibility for donor relationship development.
Advanced experience managing a staff team and in creating and directing team-wide strategy.
Advanced experience in securing strategic partnership agreements to advance an organization’s mission.
Highly organized with an attention to detail that ensures successful tracking, management, and engaged donor relationships.
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to represent the organization and its work to donors as well as interface with a rich diversity of donors, volunteers, and staff while maintaining tact, diplomacy, and confidentiality.
Impeccable attention to detail and effective writing, editing, and verbal communication skills.
Adept with Mac operating systems, Google Suite, and MS Office Suite (especially Excel, Powerpoint and Word) and donor databases, preferably Salesforce.
Experience supervising people in a way that acknowledges differentials in privilege and power, recognizes their gifts, encourages their confidence, supports their growth, and holds them accountable to standards and achieving collective goals.
Commitment to the beliefs and values of Essie with a demonstrated passion for Black feminism and progressive politics, specifically in gender justice, race justice and ending mass incarceration.

Qualities

A uniquely skilled, empathetic communicator. You are someone who uses your highly developed sense of empathy to tap into what motivates others to act. Because of your belief that everyone benefits from the type of future for which our membership fights, you find ways to make meaningful connections to our work for individuals who may not have had any direct experience with poverty, incarceration, or race, gender, or heteronormative bias.
Immaculately organized in approach. You understand that coordinating multiple projects with complex data necessitates an efficient process. You feel comfortable creating and utilizing project management systems that ensure deadlines and details aren’t missed.
Discernment and honesty we can trust. You are a thoughtful team member who acts in alignment with your integrity and are unfailingly trustworthy. You earn rather than demand the trust of people by listening and making decisions thoughtfully.
Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate.
Uplifting and additive. You see mistakes as opportunities for growth, problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a positive approach, can-do attitude, and authentic kindness wherever you go.

The Position

The Associate Director of Development is a full-time, salaried, exempt position. This position is supervised by the Interim Co-Executive Director. The salary for this position is between $110k-$120k depending on experience with full medical, dental, and vision benefits, optional 401(k), a substantial vacation package, and a monthly personal wellness stipend. The position is based in one of Essie’s offices in Oakland or Los Angeles, California.

To Apply

Please address a personal, specific, and thoughtful cover letter to the “Essie Hiring Committee” and submit along with a resume through our hiring portal (https://essiejusticegroup.bamboohr.com/jobs). Your resume tells us what you can do; your cover letter should tell us who you are and why you want to work with Essie.

Essie Justice Group provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all staff members. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and skills. Essie does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, immigration status, socioeconomic status, ancestry, age, size, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, familial status, veteran status, disability, AIDS/HIV status, medical condition, prior conviction, arrest history, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Essie values and specifically seeks applicants who are people with incarcerated loved ones; formerly incarcerated people; people of color; women; queer, transgender, gender expansive, and gender fluid people.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, performance assessment, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

About Essie Justice Group

Essie Justice Group is a non profit organization of women with incarcerated loved ones taking on the rampant injustices created by mass incarceration. Our award-winning Healing to Advocacy Model brings women together to heal, build collective power, and drive social change. Essie is

jobs.description:
Organization Overview

The School of American Ballet (SAB) at Lincoln Center, founded by George Balanchine and Lincoln Kirstein, is the preeminent ballet school in the country. Our mission is to train professional dancers for careers in classical ballet. We provide the resources for a diverse pool of students to train at the highest level - with 15-25 a year going on to dance for New York City Ballet, our official but independent ballet company, and other major ballet companies worldwide. SAB has a far-reaching impact on the art form and enriches the lives of each student who comes through its doors, over 800 annually, ages 6 to 18. SAB has approximately 90 part- and full-time employees and an operating budget of $17 million. In the 2025-2026 school year, administrative employees are expected to work in person 4 days per week and may telecommute one day per work week.

Position Overview

The School of American Ballet (SAB) seeks a Director of Institutional Giving to lead and expand its robust institutional giving program, comprised of foundation, government, and corporate foundation giving components. As a member of the School's development staff, the Director of Institutional Giving will be responsible for raising over $1.5 million annually, plus additional capital and endowment fundraising as needed. This position leads and grows the School's institutional fundraising and is a leader and resource for department-wide staff and volunteers. The Director of Institutional Giving directly supervises and mentors one staff member.  This is a full-time, exempt position reporting to the Chief Development and Marketing Officer.

Key Responsibilities

Institutional Giving

Manage and expand the School's institutional giving strategy to secure more than $1.5 million, with gifts ranging from $1,000 to $250,000+. 
Build and manage relationships with 40+ foundations, corporate, and government donors to ensure strong engagement with SAB and steward lasting support. 
Identify and strategically cultivate institutional prospects; implement tailored engagement strategies; solicit and secure gifts personally and as part of a team; and steward donors to maintain and strengthen long-term relationships. 
Work closely with SAB-wide staff to conceive of and submit persuasive, well-written, and applicable proposals and reports, with accompanying budgets and support materials, on behalf of student life programming, the scholarship fund, and other priority initiatives. 
Oversee a comprehensive donor communication strategy, ensuring timely and high-quality engagement through acknowledgement letters, written correspondence, invitations, mailings, visits, calls, newsletters, and e-blasts. 
Develop strong relationships with Board members and coworkers; engage the Board's Development Committee in cultivating and stewarding institutional donors; and serve as a resource to the Board and senior leadership team in their fundraising efforts. 
Guide prospect solicitation and donor stewardship efforts by the Executive Director and Board through the preparation of research, talking points, email drafts, and meeting briefings. 
Partner on the planning, execution, and fundraising for future capital and endowment campaigns. 

Supervision

Mentor, train, and supervise staff in Institutional Giving to ensure that departmental goals and needs are being met, and that staff are continually developing in their roles. 
Oversee the work conducted on behalf of Institutional Giving by department staff and volunteers. 
Supervise the maintenance of tracking systems, Institutional Giving mailing lists, and electronic and physical donor records. 
Manage Institutional Giving's expense budget. 

Requirements

Qualifications

5+ years of demonstrated success in institutional giving; knowledge of New York area funders. 
Excellent written and oral communication skills; fluency in budgeting and data analysis; ability to manage time and projects in a fast-paced environment. 
Proven track record of securing institutional gifts at the $100,000+ level. 
Polished and professional demeanor, with the ability to speak on behalf of the School at events. 
Proficiency in Raiser's Edge or a similar donor database. 
Tasks might include some lifting, including heavy items that require use of carts. 
Evening and weekend hours required for donor events. 

Benefits

SAB offers a superior benefit package, including full health benefits, four weeks of vacation (plus two holiday weeks in December), and generous retirement savings benefits.

The School of American Ballet is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Diverse candidates are encouraged to apply.

The annual salary range is $100,000-$112,000.

Request for Proposals (RFP) for Regional Executive Director

New York City Metro Design-Build Institute of America

1. Introduction

The New York City Metro Region of the Design-Build Institute of America (DBIA) is seeking proposals from qualified individuals or firms to provide executive leadership and management services as the Regional Executive Director (ED). The selected contractor will oversee the administration, financial management, and program development for the region, ensuring alignment with DBIA’s mission and objectives. This position will report to the Regional Board of Directors. 

2. Mission Statement

To promote the value of integrated design-build project delivery and teach the effective implementation of design and construction services to ensure success for Owners and design and construction practitioners. 

3. Background

DBIA is a leading organization dedicated to advancing design-build project delivery. The NYC Metro Region serves as a critical hub for industry professionals, providing education, advocacy, and networking opportunities. The ED will be instrumental in executing the region’s strategic vision and fostering strong relationships with members, volunteers, and stakeholders. 

4. Scope of Work

The selected ED will be responsible for the following key areas: 

4.1 Regional Governance

Advise and support the Regional Board of Directors and Executive Council. 
Attend and coordinate a quarterly virtual Regional Board of Directors meetings, including agenda preparation, attendance meeting minutes, and follow-up actions. 
Attend virtual monthly Committee Coordination Meeting, capture attendance, meeting minutes, and follow-up actions. 
Develop, maintain, and manage the regional annual events calendar.  
Provide guidance and support to Board members, committees, and volunteers. 
Manage Region online collaboration tool and file management system, Basecamp currently in use.  
Ensure compliance with DBIA bylaws, policies, and governance standards. 

4.2 Financial Management

Develop and manage the region’s annual budget and cash flow in collaboration with the Board. 
Oversee financial reporting, audits, and 990 tax filings. 
Administer resources within approved budgets and financial guidelines. 
Identify opportunities for revenue diversification, including sponsorships and programs. 

4.3 Membership Growth & Engagement

Implement strategies for membership recruitment and retention in collaboration with DBIA National. 
Monitor membership metrics and adjust strategies accordingly. 
Maintain accurate membership records and respond to member inquiries. 
Develop and execute strategies to maximize member engagement, including the support of our Student Chapters. 

4.4 Program & Event Management

In collaboration with the Education Committee, assist in the planning and execution of regional events, including conferences, awards programs, and educational sessions.  
Develop professional development and training opportunities in alignment with DBIA National standards. 
Ensure event success, attendance, sponsorship, and financial performance goals are met. 

4.5 Communications & Marketing

Manage regional communication channels, including newsletters, websites, and social media. 
Develop marketing campaigns and event advertisements to promote regional initiatives and programs. 
Serve as the regional spokesperson as needed. 
Ensure all event-related materials, forms, and flyers are accurate and aligned with DBIA standards.  
Perform advertising, registration, and logistical services for 12 regional in-person 2-hour programs, 4 2-hour virtual programs, a golf tournament (108 golfers), and a 2-day annual conference. 
Serve as primary point of contact between member communication in region and liaison to National. region. 

4.6 Sponsorship & Fundraising

Identify and cultivate relationships with sponsors and partners. 
Develop sponsorship packages and fundraising initiatives in collaboration with the Board. 

4.7 Platforms & Applications

The Vice President of Development will secure funding for both annual operating needs and targeted programmatic or capital projects, while serving as a visible ambassador for Embarc Collective’s mission across the Tampa Bay and state of Florida business and philanthropic community.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a leader who is energized by mission-driven work, excited to build something new, and eager to play a significant role in shaping the startup and venture ecosystem in Tampa Bay and across the state. The Vice President of Development is expected to be equally comfortable writing a grant proposal, making a major gift ask to a donor, and representing the organization to diverse audiences, including corporate executives and university leadership, elected officials and policymakers, major donors and other funders, investors, and media. Finally, the right candidate will collaborate closely with Embarc Collective’s Vice President of Finance and Administration and external legal counsel on contract strategy and execution, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO and board of directors.

This role is on-site and structured within a 40-hour workweek, but there will be some after-5 pm work events required, so your schedule may fluctuate on a week-to-week basis.

About Embarc Collective

Embarc Collective, a 501c3 not-for-profit and Florida’s largest and fastest growing startup hub, is a central landing zone for some of the most driven and focused startup builders in Florida. Founded to address a critical gap in Florida’s innovation infrastructure, Embarc Collective provides a comprehensive platform of programming, community, and resources designed to give early-stage tech founders every advantage.

Embarc Collective’s startup platform offers founders curated programming and a constantly-growing repository of startup resources and frameworks, on-demand coaching and mentorship, access to tech and tech-enabled talent, connectivity to corporates, universities, and investors, workspace, assigned offices, conference rooms and event space in our 32,000 sq ft hub in downtown Tampa, and engagement with a peer community of 330+ founders and founding team members that lead 145+ Florida-based early-stage tech startups and growth-stage companies in sixty sectors, including healthcare and life sciences, medical devices and robotics, cybersecurity and data analytics, AI and frontier tech, fintech and legaltech, edtech, renewable energy and climate tech, and defense and national security, among others.

Embarc Collective also hosts more than 350 events annually that draw 11,500+ participants into entrepreneurship, technology, and innovation conversations in downtown Tampa. In addition, more than 20,000 professionals, including hundreds of seed, venture, and growth equity investors, visit Embarc each year to engage with founders in our community and the high growth tech companies they lead, marking our efforts to demonstrate the vibrancy and strength of Tampa Bay’s startup and innovation ecosystem and helping lead the way for Tampa Bay and the state of Florida on the national and international stage.

What we’re looking for:

At least ten (10) years of experience in progressive fundraising, grant writing, or corporate relations experience, ideally within an economic development, startup hub or entrepreneurial support organization, or tech-adjacent nonprofit, with a demonstrated track record of securing significant gifts from individual donors, corporations and universities, institutional investors and service providers, philanthropic foundations, and local, state, and federal government agencies and related entities .

Excellent written and verbal communication skills and people skills.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Ability to manage and work with different personalities/work styles.
Highly organized, self-directed, and action oriented.
Thrive in a fast-paced startup setting where adaptability is essential.
Driven, initiative-taking, enthusiastic and with a “can do” attitude.
Experience in or a genuine connection to the Tampa Bay region and/or state of Florida is a plus; a willingness to be deeply embedded in the local ecosystem is a must.
Bachelor’s degree is required (preferably in business, marketing, public relations, or strategic communications); Master’s degree is preferred.

jobs.description:
The Baltimore School for the Arts Foundation is the 501c(3) fundraising partner of the Baltimore School for the Arts (BSA), a Baltimore City Public High School, and the TWIGS (To Work in Gaining Skills) program for Baltimore City youth grades 2-8. Created in 1980, the Foundation has grown from a small annual fundraising organization to one that manages 100+ part-time arts faculty, a strong endowment, and multiple project-based budgets with a $4.2 million annual budget.

As the Director of Development, you will join an enthusiastic, collaborative team of professionals committed to the mission and vision of the BSA. BSA is a focused, fast-paced and supportive work environment committed to diversity and equity in all aspects of our work. We intend to recruit and support an inclusive staff who will enable BSA to continue evolving to serve a diverse city better.

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting to and partnering with the Foundation Director, the Director of Development is responsible for the planning, management, and growth of the Foundation’s annual operating fund. This includes overseeing the year-round coordination of donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Director of Development manages the daily fundraising operations of the Foundation, overseeing the Development Associate and Alumni Liaison and working closely with the Grant Writer. The successful candidate will enhance the team’s capacity to sustain relationships with its many donors and attract new supporters.

Primary Responsibilities

Maintain a portfolio of individual donors, family foundations, and prospects of meaningful capacity by utilizing fundraising best practices, with a heavy focus on in-person solicitations, to help the Foundation achieve short and long-term fundraising goals.
Grow the individual donor base by identifying, qualifying, cultivating, and soliciting new prospects, moving them through the pipeline in an intentional, systematic, and authentic way.
Develop and maintain ongoing relationships with major donors ($3,500+).
Develop bold giving and engagement strategies through a collaborative process with the Foundation team and BSA colleagues, based on research and relationships.
Supervise and work closely with the Development Associate to ensure the integrity of BSA’s donor database, Raiser’s Edge.
Supervise and work closely with the Alumni Liaison to implement engaging and impactful alumni giving programs, communications, and events.
Facilitate conversations with BSA staff and faculty to identify programs and initiatives that require funding or may be of interest to potential prospects. Connect with colleagues to secure relevant project information, including budgets, to create proposals.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Foundation Director to create donor strategies, campaigns, and initiatives to achieve community-wide goals.
Actively contribute to BSA’s equity-informed and inclusive work environment by taking an active role in promoting practices that support diversity, inclusion, and belonging.
Assist with events for the Foundation, BSA, and TWIGS, including BSA’s annual fundraising event, Expressions.
Other duties in collaboration with the Foundation team as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS

The Foundation seeks someone for this role who has the energy, enthusiasm, and desire to make a real difference in the BSA’s fundraising efforts. The Director of Development will be a strategic thinker who anticipates needs, contributes creative ideas, and proposes solutions with strong decision-making capability; taking initiative to investigate and resolve questions.

Preferred

A minimum of 5 years of professional fundraising work or equivalent experience.
Experience with Raiser's Edge is preferred.
Management experience is preferred.
Passion for the mission of the Baltimore School for the Arts.
Eagerness to grow as a fundraising professional and willing to tackle opportunities and special projects as needed.
Knowledgeable on a variety of fundraising strategies and methods. Experienced in planning and implementing long- and short-range goals to meet established priorities.
Proficiency in listening to understand donor motivations and build trusted relationships.
Ability to manage time, resources, and workload to maximize productivity and financial results, while maintaining a clear view of how each advances the institution's mission.
Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to present effectively one-on-one and to small groups.
High level of tact and diplomacy with donors, board members, volunteers, and staff at all levels.
Ability to foster teamwork and work cooperatively with others to set goals, resolve problems and make decisions that enhance organizational effectiveness.
Adept at relationships with people of various identities and cultures.

ABOUT THE POSITION

The Director of Development position is a full-time exempt, hybrid position with a salary range of $85,000-$91,000 commensurate with experience and qualifications.
The Foundation offers a choice of 3 different health plans and pays for 75% of the insurance premium for the employee and their dependent children on the least expensive plan.
403b plan is available with pre-tax contribution eligibility.
All employees are entitled to 4 weeks of vacation, 6 sick days, and 9 paid holidays, in addition to Winter Break, Spring Break, and the following BCPSS Holidays: 4th of July, Labor Day, Election Day (during election years), Thanksgiving, The day after Thanksgiving, Martin Luther King’s Birthday, President’s Day, Memorial Day, and Juneteenth

If a holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the Foundation will determine on which day the holiday will be observed.

Interested applicants should send a resume and brief letter of interest to the attention of Stephanie Moore, Foundation Director at smoore@bsfa.org.

new_jobs.title: Vice President of Development
new_jobs.description:
Embarc Collective, a 501c3 non-profit and the state of Florida’s leading startup hub, invites applications for the position of Vice President of Development.

As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, our work depends on the generosity of corporate and university partners, philanthropic donors, and community investors who share our vision for a thriving Tampa Bay innovation economy. The Vice President of Development will lead the organization’s full range of fundraising activities, including gifts from individuals, corporations and universities, government, and foundation sources for annual operating needs as well as programmatic or capital projects. This is a pivotal moment in Embarc Collective's growth — and we are seeking a seasoned fundraising leader to help us seize it.

The Opportunity

The Vice President of Development is a newly created leadership role that will define and execute Embarc Collective's fundraising strategy and a significant organizational investment — a signal of Embarc Collective’s commitment to building a sustainable, diversified funding base to power its next chapter of growth. This leader will be responsible for establishing and maintaining Embarc Collective’s development strategy, infrastructure, and relationships needed to raise funds from individual donors, corporations and universities, institutional investors and service providers, philanthropic foundations, and local, state, and federal government agencies and related entities. The Vice President of Development will secure funding for both annual operating needs and targeted programmatic or capital projects, while serving as a visible ambassador for Embarc Collective’s mission across the Tampa Bay and state of Florida business and philanthropic community.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a leader who is energized by mission-driven work, excited to build something new, and eager to play a significant role in shaping the startup and venture ecosystem in Tampa Bay and across the state. The Vice President of Development is expected to be equally comfortable writing a grant proposal, making a major gift ask to a donor, and representing the organization to diverse audiences, including corporate executives and university leadership, elected officials and policymakers, major donors and other funders, investors, and media. Finally, the right candidate will collaborate closely with Embarc Collective’s Vice President of Finance and Administration and external legal counsel on contract strategy and execution, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO and board of directors.

This role is on-site and structured within a 40-hour workweek, but there will be some after-5 pm work events required, so your schedule may fluctuate on a week-to-week basis.

About Embarc Collective

Embarc Collective, a 501c3 not-for-profit and Florida’s largest and fastest growing startup hub, is a central landing zone for some of the most driven and focused startup builders in Florida. Founded to address a critical gap in Florida’s innovation infrastructure, Embarc Collective provides a comprehensive platform of programming, community, and resources designed to give early-stage tech founders every advantage.

Embarc Collective’s startup platform offers founders curated programming and a constantly-growing repository of startup resources and frameworks, on-demand coaching and mentorship, access to tech and tech-enabled talent, connectivity to corporates, universities, and investors, workspace, assigned offices, conference rooms and event space in our 32,000 sq ft hub in downtown Tampa, and engagement with a peer community of 330+ founders and founding team members that lead 145+ Florida-based early-stage tech startups and growth-stage companies in sixty sectors, including healthcare and life sciences, medical devices and robotics, cybersecurity and data analytics, AI and frontier tech, fintech and legaltech, edtech, renewable energy and climate tech, and defense and national security, among others.

Embarc Collective also hosts more than 350 events annually that draw 11,500+ participants into entrepreneurship, technology, and innovation conversations in downtown Tampa. In addition, more than 20,000 professionals, including hundreds of seed, venture, and growth equity investors, visit Embarc each year to engage with founders in our community and the high growth tech companies they lead, marking our efforts to demonstrate the vibrancy and strength of Tampa Bay’s startup and innovation ecosystem and helping lead the way for Tampa Bay and the state of Florida on the national and international stage.

What we’re looking for:

At least ten (10) years of experience in progressive fundraising, grant writing, or corporate relations experience, ideally within an economic development, startup hub or entrepreneurial support organization, or tech-adjacent nonprofit, with a demonstrated track record of securing significant gifts from individual donors, corporations and universities, institutional investors and service providers, philanthropic foundations, and local, state, and federal government agencies and related entities .
Exceptional relationship-builder that can build trust quickly and cultivate and sustain long-term relationships with major donors, corporate sponsors, and philanthropic foundations over time and is comfortable pitching Embarc Collective’s value proposition to prospective donors and/or investors .
Ability to Identify and evaluate local, state, and federal government and private funding opportunities for annual, programmatic capital, capacity building, and special projects.
Experience conducting research and drafting grant proposals targeted at philanthropic foundations, economic development agencies, and/or local, state, and federal government agencies and related entities.
Experience identifying and tracking key performance indicators (KPIs) and reporting fundraising progress, creating and delivering customized impact reports and stewardship plans, and regularly communicating to donors to keep them informed and engaged.
Ability to “dot connect” making introductions and connections between different stakeholders (companies, investors, corporates, etc.) and to plan and execute fundraising communications strategies across all platforms.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and people skills.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Ability to manage and work with different personalities/work styles.
Highly organized, self-directed, and action oriented.
Thrive in a fast-paced startup setting where adaptability is essential.
Driven, initiative-taking, enthusiastic and with a “can do” attitude.
Experience in or a genuine connection to the Tampa Bay region and/or state of Florida is a plus; a willingness to be deeply embedded in the local ecosystem is a must.
Bachelor’s degree is required (preferably in business, marketing, public relations, or strategic communications); Master’s degree is preferred.

If this sounds like you, we want to connect:

You have demonstrated success in developing and managing relations with prospective donors and personally closing philanthropic commitments.
You have experience developing and executing a multi-year fundraising strategy, identifying and vetting prospective donors, setting annual fundraising goals across different funding sources, and tracking progress against both operating and programmatic or capital project targets.
You combine strategic thinking with a strong bias for execution.
You have an inventive mind that can articulate the value of contributing to an organization whose mission is to engage, serve, and support a community of driven, focused startup builders and can set a vision and roll up your sleeves to make it happen.
You are a strong relationship-builder.
You excel at building trust, unifying teams around a shared vision, and driving organizational impact and performance by ensuring clear, consistent messaging and you can sustain those relationships over time.
You are a compelling communicator and comfortable in public settings.
You are comfortable representing Embarc Collective to diverse audiences including elected officials and policymakers, major donors and other funders, corporate executives and university leadership, investors, and media.

You are deeply curious about the startup and venture landscape.
You are excited to support Embarc Collective’s mission and help position Florida as a leading hub for tech startups; you remain current on funding trends, emerging sectors, and the evolving needs of founders; and you’re eager to learn about ecosystem building that advances innovation and the broader startup community.
You thrive in a collaborative environment.
This role requires collaborating closely with team members across the organization, and you have a record of success in teamwork and managing multiple projects simultaneously in a mission-driven environment.

Compensation package that is competitive with the market and commensurate with experience, including base salary, performance bonus eligibility, and benefits package. We strongly encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

new_jobs.description:
At FNBO, our employees are the heart of our story—and we’re committed to their success! Please see below the details of this career opportunity and how it fits into our organization’s success.

Summary Of The Job

This role is responsible for leading business development strategy, sales execution, and market expansion across two critical growth businesses within FNBO. This role drives revenue growth through the acquisition of strategic clients, development of high-performing business development teams, and execution of growth strategies that strengthen FNBO's market position.

The role has broad accountability for two distinct business lines, the majority of the role is supporting Home Improvement Lending.

Home Improvement Lending (HIL) – Leading a team responsible for acquiring and expanding relationships with contractors, dealers, and organizations that offer FNBO lending solutions to consumers seeking financing for home improvement projects.
Card Personalization Solutions – Leading a business development associate responsible for acquiring organizations that require card issuance and personalization services, including gift cards, debit cards, credit cards, and related payment card solutions.

This role develops and executes business growth strategies, establishes long-term client acquisition plans, manages business development resources, and influences outcomes across multiple departments and stakeholders. In addition to leading business development for HIL and Card Personalization, they will also play a leadership role in the overall business development team including the Cobrand and Financial Institution credit card business development space. This position contributes to the long-term growth strategy of the full business while ensuring annual revenue, client acquisition, and profitability objectives are achieved.

About This Role

Strategic Leadership

Develop and execute annual and multi-year business development strategies for POS Lending and Card Personalization businesses.
Identify emerging market opportunities, industry trends, and competitive threats that may impact business performance.
Establish growth priorities, target markets, and client acquisition strategies that drive sustainable revenue expansion in alignment with the organization’s growth objectives.
Direct strategic planning activities and establish measurable performance indicators supporting business objectives.

Revenue Growth & Market Expansion

Own growth outcomes across both business lines, including new client acquisition, pipeline development, market penetration, and revenue generation.
Direct business development efforts aimed at expanding FNBO's presence in the home improvement financing ecosystem by leading market expansion initiatives to secure contractors, dealers, distributors, and affinity organizations that can offer FNBO financing solutions.
Drive growth within the Card Personalization business by securing new issuer, fintech, program manager, and corporate relationships.
Identify and pursue complex, high-value opportunities that significantly impact business results.

Business Development Leadership

Lead and develop high-performing business development teams responsible for sourcing, qualifying, negotiating, and closing new business opportunities.
Establish sales processes, client acquisition standards, and performance expectations that drive consistent results.
Monitor pipeline health, forecast business performance, and implement strategies to address performance gaps.

Client & Partner Relationship Management

Develop executive-level relationships with prospective clients, strategic partners, industry influencers, and key stakeholders.
Serve as an executive representative for FNBO with external organizations and industry associations.
Lead negotiations for large, complex, and strategically important client opportunities.
Partner with legal, credit, operations, technology, risk, finance, marketing, and product teams to successfully onboard and support new clients.
Ensure long-term client satisfaction and retention through strategic relationship oversight.

Financial & Operational Leadership

Develop and manage operating plans that support business growth objectives.
Allocate financial and talent resources across business development functions to maximize performance and return on investment.
Evaluate growth opportunities using financial, operational, and market-based analysis.
Ensure business development activities operate within risk, compliance, and governance requirements.

Cross-Functional Influence

Drive collaboration across product, operations, technology, marketing, risk, finance, and executive leadership teams.
Influence decisions impacting business strategy, capacity planning, product development, and client experience.
Lead resolution of complex business challenges that affect growth, client acquisition, and operational execution.
Represent business development priorities in executive discussions and planning forums.

Required

The Ideal Candidate for This Role:

Bachelor’s degree required; MBA preferred
10+ years in sales, business development, or financial services
5+ years in senior leadership roles
Experience building, developing and leading large, distributed, high-performing teams
Experience launching and scaling new business opportunities
Strong background in building and managing strategic partnerships
Experience managing revenue goals or P&L
Strong executive presence and ability to influence stakeholders
Frequent travel required

Candidates must possess unrestricted work authorization and not require future sponsorship.

Regardless of your location, you'll be fully integrated into our team through robust digital collaboration tools and regular communication. The incumbent can work remotely from any of the states listed on the job posting, though occasional travel may be required for in-person meetings. new_jobs.description:
The Baltimore School for the Arts Foundation is the 501c(3) fundraising partner of the Baltimore School for the Arts (BSA), a Baltimore City Public High School, and the TWIGS (To Work in Gaining Skills) program for Baltimore City youth grades 2-8. Created in 1980, the Foundation has grown from a small annual fundraising organization to one that manages 100+ part-time arts faculty, a strong endowment, and multiple project-based budgets with a $4.2 million annual budget.

As the Director of Development, you will join an enthusiastic, collaborative team of professionals committed to the mission and vision of the BSA. BSA is a focused, fast-paced and supportive work environment committed to diversity and equity in all aspects of our work. We intend to recruit and support an inclusive staff who will enable BSA to continue evolving to serve a diverse city better.

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting to and partnering with the Foundation Director, the Director of Development is responsible for the planning, management, and growth of the Foundation’s annual operating fund. This includes overseeing the year-round coordination of donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Director of Development manages the daily fundraising operations of the Foundation, overseeing the Development Associate and Alumni Liaison and working closely with the Grant Writer. The successful candidate will enhance the team’s capacity to sustain relationships with its many donors and attract new supporters.

Primary Responsibilities

Maintain a portfolio of individual donors, family foundations, and prospects of meaningful capacity by utilizing fundraising best practices, with a heavy focus on in-person solicitations, to help the Foundation achieve short and long-term fundraising goals.
Grow the individual donor base by identifying, qualifying, cultivating, and soliciting new prospects, moving them through the pipeline in an intentional, systematic, and authentic way.
Develop and maintain ongoing relationships with major donors ($3,500+).
Develop bold giving and engagement strategies through a collaborative process with the Foundation team and BSA colleagues, based on research and relationships.
Supervise and work closely with the Development Associate to ensure the integrity of BSA’s donor database, Raiser’s Edge.
Supervise and work closely with the Alumni Liaison to implement engaging and impactful alumni giving programs, communications, and events.
Facilitate conversations with BSA staff and faculty to identify programs and initiatives that require funding or may be of interest to potential prospects. Connect with colleagues to secure relevant project information, including budgets, to create proposals.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Foundation Director to create donor strategies, campaigns, and initiatives to achieve community-wide goals.
Actively contribute to BSA’s equity-informed and inclusive work environment by taking an active role in promoting practices that support diversity, inclusion, and belonging.
Assist with events for the Foundation, BSA, and TWIGS, including BSA’s annual fundraising event, Expressions.
Other duties in collaboration with the Foundation team as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS

The Foundation seeks someone for this role who has the energy, enthusiasm, and desire to make a real difference in the BSA’s fundraising efforts. The Director of Development will be a strategic thinker who anticipates needs, contributes creative ideas, and proposes solutions with strong decision-making capability; taking initiative to investigate and resolve questions.

Preferred

A minimum of 5 years of professional fundraising work or equivalent experience.
Experience with Raiser's Edge is preferred.
Management experience is preferred.
Passion for the mission of the Baltimore School for the Arts.
Eagerness to grow as a fundraising professional and willing to tackle opportunities and special projects as needed.
Knowledgeable on a variety of fundraising strategies and methods. Experienced in planning and implementing long- and short-range goals to meet established priorities.
Proficiency in listening to understand donor motivations and build trusted relationships.
Ability to manage time, resources, and workload to maximize productivity and financial results, while maintaining a clear view of how each advances the institution's mission.
Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to present effectively one-on-one and to small groups.
High level of tact and diplomacy with donors, board members, volunteers, and staff at all levels.
Ability to foster teamwork and work cooperatively with others to set goals, resolve problems and make decisions that enhance organizational effectiveness.
Adept at relationships with people of various identities and cultures.

ABOUT THE POSITION

The Director of Development position is a full-time exempt, hybrid position with a salary range of $85,000-$91,000 commensurate with experience and qualifications.
The Foundation offers a choice of 3 different health plans and pays for 75% of the insurance premium for the employee and their dependent children on the least expensive plan.
403b plan is available with pre-tax contribution eligibility.
All employees are entitled to 4 weeks of vacation, 6 sick days, and 9 paid holidays, in addition to Winter Break, Spring Break, and the following BCPSS Holidays: 4th of July, Labor Day, Election Day (during election years), Thanksgiving, The day after Thanksgiving, Martin Luther King’s Birthday, President’s Day, Memorial Day, and Juneteenth

If a holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the Foundation will determine on which day the holiday will be observed.

Interested applicants should send a resume and brief letter of interest to the attention of Stephanie Moore, Foundation Director at smoore@bsfa.org.

Risk Management
: Identify and address potential risks to project timelines, budgets, and quality, working with internal teams and external partners to mitigate issues.
Collaboration with Internal Teams
: Work closely with the property management and operations teams to ensure developments are designed with operational efficiency and resident satisfaction in mind.
Project Reporting
: Regularly report project progress to senior leadership, providing updates on budget, timelines, and any changes to the scope of the project.
Community Engagement
: Engage with local stakeholders, including residents, community organizations, and local government agencies, to foster positive relationships and ensure developments align with community needs.
Post-Development Review
: Oversee the handoff process once the project is completed, ensuring the property meets operational standards and is ready for occupancy.

: Bachelor’s degree in Real Estate, Construction Management, Urban Planning, Business, or related field. A Master’s degree is a plus.

: 5+ years of experience in real estate development, project management, or construction management, preferably within affordable housing.
Familiarity with Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) projects and financing is strongly preferred.

:
Strong understanding of project management principles, financial modeling, and budgeting.
Ability to oversee multiple projects concurrently while maintaining high attention to detail.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and project management software (e.g., MS Project, Procore).
Knowledge of zoning, building codes, and construction regulations.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to address project issues in a timely manner.

Certifications
: Project Management Professional (PMP) or similar certification is a plus.

required.

Mission-Driven Work

Employee Assistance Plan for you and your immediate family.
